KYRIACOS LOUCA JR., DPA kyriacosloucair@gmail.com Dear Dr. Louca, Jr., www.dil . ov. h —e-g—P— 2025 This refers to your electronic mail dated 26 February 2025, requesting clarification on the individuals authorized to administer oaths pursuant to Republic Act No. 6733, as amended by Republic Act No. 10755. With respect to your query on whether the Head of the Office for Senior Citizens Affairs (OSCA) and the Local Social Welfare and Development Officer (LSWDO) under the Local Government Unit (LGU) are vested with general authority to administer oaths under Republic Act No. 67331, as amended by Republic Act No. 107552, it is important to examine the aforementioned laws in conjunction with other relevant statutes3, rules4, and regulations. After careful scrutiny, it is noted that neither RA 6733 nor RA 10755 explicitly grants the authority to administer oaths to the OSCA Head or the LSWDO. Verily, the power to administer oaths is conferred to and generally reserved for specific public officers, notaries public and certain officials authorized by law. Likewise, while Republic Act No. 71605 grants the power to administer oaths to certain local government officials, such as Assessors6, Assistant Assessors7, members of the Local Board of Assessment AppealsS, 1 AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION 21, TITLE 1, BOOK I OF THE REVISED ADMINISTRATIVE CODE AND SECTION 41, BOOK I OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987, GRANTING MEMBERS OF BOTH HOUSES OF THE CONGRESS OF THE PHILIPPINES THE GENERAL AUTHORITY TO ADMINISTER OATHS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES. AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE PUNONG BARANGAY TO ADMINISTER THE OATH OF OFFICE OF ANY GOVERNMENT OFFICIAL, INCLUDING THE PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 41 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6733. 3 EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, July 25, 1987 (ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987). '1 Section I, Rule 138 of the Rules of Court. LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991. 6 SECTION 213. Authority of Assessor to Take Evidence. - For the purpose of obtaining information on which to base the market value of any real property, the assessor of the province, city or municipality or his deputy may summon the owners of the properties to be affected or persons having legal interest therein and witnesses, administer oaths, and take deposition concerning the property, its ownership, amount, nature, and value. 7 SECTION 473. Assistant Assessor. - (a) x x x (b) The assistant assessor shall assist the assessor and perform such other duties as the latter may assign to him. He shall have the authority to administer oaths on all declarations of real property for purposes of assessments. 8 SECTION 229. Action by the Local Board of Assessment Appeals. - (a) x x x (b) In the exercise of its appellate jurisdiction, the Board shall have the power to summon witnesses, administer oaths, conduct ocular inspection, take depositions, and issue subpoena and subpoena duces tecum. The proceedings of the Board shall be "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Tel. (02) 8876-3454

Punong Barangays and Lupon members9, and Assistant Treasurers10, this power is strictly limited to their respective official functions and does not extend to the OSCA Head or LSWDO. Thus, given that the OSCA Head and LSWDO are not designated as oath administrators under the abovementioned laws, they do not possess the general authority to administer oaths as part of their official duties. With regard to your second query—whether the Sangguniang Bayan or Sangguniang Panlungsod may, by ordinance or resolution, confer such authority—it bears emphasizing that local legislative enactments must conform to the Constitution and national statutes. 11 This principle was clearly articulated in the case of City of Batangas v. Philippine Shell Petroleum Corporation12, where the Court emphasized that "municipal ordinances are inferior in status and subordinate to the laws of the state." The Court further stated that any ordinance conflicting with a state law of general application is invalid and that local authorities cannot adopt ordinances that contradict the spirit of state laws or are inconsistent with the general policy of the state. Thus, while LGUs, through their respective legislative councils, do exercise delegated legislative powers13, these powers are limited and must conform to the will of their principal, the State. 14 Irrefragably, the authority to administer oaths is a specific legal power that is not generally bestowed to all public officers but rather granted by explicit provisions of the law. Consequently, it is this Department's opinion that while the Sanggunian may pass an ordinance to confer certain powers upon local officers, such an ordinance cannot grant authority that contradicts or conflicts with national laws. Simply put, it must be clearly aligned with national legislation and cannot extend beyond what is explicitly authorized by law. Therefore, any ordinance seeking to grant the power to administer oaths to the OSCA Head or LSWDO would need to be carefully reviewed to ensure it is consistent with existing statutes, such as the Revised Administrative Code, its amendments, and RA 7160. conducted solely for the purpose of ascertaining the facts without necessarily adhering to technical rules applicable in judicial proceedings. 9 SECTION 420. Power to Administer Oaths. - The punong barangay, as chairman of the lupong tagapamayapa, and the members of the pangkat are hereby authorized to administer oaths in connection with any matter relating to all proceedings in the implementation of the katarungang pambarangay. 10 SECTION 471. Assistant Treasurer. - (a) x x x (b) x x x (c) The assistant treasurer shall assist the treasurer and perform such duties as the latter may assign to him. He shall have authority to administer oaths concerning notices and notifications to those delinquents in the payment of real property tax and concerning Official matters relating to the accounts of the treasurer or otherwise arising in the offices of the treasurer and the assessor.
